preceding_messages.speaker: X
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the observer/transcriber separation and the five-entry Monday spot-audit verbatim; they close the keyboard-transposition hole at its source rather than relying on the hash to detect corruption it cannot. For the graduated-cylinder winter read specifically, I require that any observer whose initials have not yet appeared on three supervised 02:00 readings—each with the certifier's concurrent reading and a delta ≤ 0.1 mm water-equivalent—may not log frozen-precipitation entries independently until that threshold is met. The failure this prevents: a first-week volunteer reads the meniscus apex rather than the base, introducing a +0.3 mm/event bias that over four winter events produces a +1.2 mm seasonal overcount—below the ±2 mm weekly precipitation comparison tolerance I now mandate—so no persistence alert fires, the instrument is perfectly healthy at every monthly cross-check, and a year-three appendix audit surfaces a twelve-millimetre phantom accumulation attributable to no serial number, no bridging line, and no post-compilation edit. I therefore print the certifier's initials alongside the volunteer's on every graduated-cylinder entry until the three-reading threshold is cleared, and any site whose 02:00 entries lack that pairing for more than one week triggers the same formal review as the thirty-percent zero-speed wind rule.

preceding_messages.speaker: Y
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the three-reading certification threshold, the ±2 mm weekly precipitation comparison tolerance, and the certifier-initials pairing rule verbatim; they make the meniscus-geometry bias detectable at week one rather than surfacing as a year-three phantom tied to no serial number. The unresolved question your graduated-cylinder entry now raises is the solid-to-water-equivalent conversion: I mandate that every 02:00 reading pair with a simultaneous full-depth density measurement using a spring-loaded density plate (±5 kg/m³ resolution) pressed to the accumulation base, and that the compiler derives water-equivalent as (solid depth × measured density) / 1000 rather than applying a fixed 10:1 ratio. The concrete failure this guards against: a dry-powder week at Site 6 logs 80 mm solid snow at a true density of 80 kg/m³ (≈ 6.4 mm water-equivalent), but a blind 10:1 conversion prints 8 mm in the comparison column, deviating +2.5 mm from the NOAA station's 5.5 mm true-week reading and exceeding your ±2 mm tolerance; if the following week repeats the regime the second consecutive exceedance trips the two-week persistence gate and sends an audit crew to verify a perfectly healthy 20-inch gauge. I therefore require that any entry whose derived density falls outside the 100–600 kg/m³ realistic-snow envelope is flagged ANOMALOUS, excluded from that week's comparison column, and noted in the appendix alongside the plate's serial number so the exclusion is auditable rather than a silent omission.

target.speaker: X
target.text: I adopt the spring-loaded density-plate specification, the derived water-equivalent formula, and the 100–600 kg/m³ ANOMALOUS exclusion verbatim; they make the solid-to-liquid conversion traceable to a measured quantity rather than an assumed ratio. For the plate's own integrity I require a monthly calibration against a certified 5 kg ice reference block seated on the plate's own load cell, with a ±10 kg/m³ tolerance before the plate is withdrawn from service and sent to a national metrology laboratory for re-springing. The concrete failure this guards against: by mid-December Site 6's plate spring has fatigued by +22 kg/m³, so every soft-snow event (true 130 kg/m³) derives a water-equivalent inflated by roughly 1.1 mm per 50 mm solid depth, and across seven winter events the accumulated overcount exceeds the ±2 mm weekly precipitation tolerance on four separate weeks yet never persists two consecutive weeks because natural density variability masks the drift week-to-week and no persistence gate fires. I therefore mandate that any site whose rolling seven-day mean derived density drifts by more than 25 kg/m³ from that site's installation-month baseline triggers an immediate plate withdrawal and metrology-lab referral, with the affected week's comparison cell printed as "PLATE CALIBRATION PENDING" rather than populated with a suspect value.
